summary: @ornikar/eslint-config-react preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package's preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) checks for a local `bun` binary and, if not present, downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases into a temp directory, unzips it, marks it executable, and invokes it against a co-shipped 727 KB file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a Bun-compiled CJS blob with obfuscator.io-style transforms (hex-named identifiers, a rotated string array constructed by `WV8StW`, a large numeric/string alphabet in `n7gIxM`, and a char-decoder `hc1jfK9`) — its content is not statically readable but is executed with full runtime privileges on the installing machine. `setup.mjs` itself is likewise obfuscated with hex identifiers (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`) and string-lookup objects that disguise ordinary node stdlib usage (`fs`, `https`, `zlib`, `execFileSync`), which has no legitimate purpose for an ESLint configuration package. An ESLint config has no reason to fetch a second language runtime or to ship and execute an obfuscated bundle at install time. The combination — install-time fetch of an alternate runtime plus execution of an opaque, obfuscated sibling bundle, plus obfuscation of the loader itself — is a supply-chain dropper that runs arbitrary code on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
